To ride the winds above the summits, to skim over white foaming 
waves, to strike as one in the heat of the hunt. There is no greater 
form of kinship with a beast than riding together.
There are certain guidelines into riding a Tamed creature and 
prerequisites to be met before one can do so.
 
• Only creatures that have been Tamed can be ridden and the 
creature must be a size larger than the Traveler.
• Mounting a creature costs 10 ft. of the Traveler's movement 
speed, while mounted, a Traveler cannot move, but can use 10 ft. 
of its movement to Dismount. A creature with 0 ft. movement 
cannot Mount or Dismount.
• If an effect moves the Traveler and their mount, or they get 
the Prone condition while mounted, they can be forcefully 
dismounted. The Traveler must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity 
Saving Throw or fall off the mount, landing Prone in a space 
within 5 ft. of it.
• In order for a Traveler to fully control a Tamed creature during 
the chaos of combat, at the Initiative roll step, the Traveler must 
roll a Animal Handling check of DC 10 + the creatures CR to a 
minimum of 1. If the Traveler fails, the creature will resort to its 
base Feral Instincts as either Aggressive, Defensive, or Wary as is 
listed on their statblock. The Traveler can attempt to control their 
beast as again as an Action on their turn.
Bonuses may be added to this Animal Handling Check
  • Add 1 to the roll for every Tamed level of the Creature
  • Add 1 to the roll if the Tamed Creature has a crafted saddle 
• Both the Traveler and the Mounted Tamed Creature act during 
the same initiative order, and the Traveler may choose which of 
them would take Actions first. A Traveler or Tamed creature must 
complete all their own Actions before the next can act.
Rise of an Alpha
While the eternal mutations of evolution are imperceivable in a life time, there are certain individuals, that stand taller, run faster 
and lead the packs to a richer season. In the wilds, it is not long before an alpha of the pack will rear its head, or the strongest hunter 
slaughters its competition, and so this advantage a creature may have over its kin can be represented by an Augmentation. 
To add to the uniqueness of an encounter, a Keeper can bestow upon a individual or excessively powerful breed of creatures an Alpha 
Augment by using the list above. There is not limit to the amount Augmentations a creature may have, as it is the Keeper's choice and 
story to tell.
Becoming the Beast
Once a creature is Tamed it becomes a permanent ally. Whether 
this relationship is one of friendship or domination is entirely 
up to the Traveler and how they choose to treat the creatures and 
world around them. 
While the creatures do not understand any language, they will 
follow simple commands from their Traveler, either verbally 
or through gestures, and with time, the creatures will begin to 
understand the directives of their Traveler like second nature.
The choice of whether or not the Traveler or the Keeper fully 
controls the Tamed creature as a Playable Character of their own, 
is up to a discussion with the Keeper and who they think is best 
suited to be responsible roleplaying the creature.
Riding Tamed Creatures
A Guiding Hand
A Tamed Creature that has survived the perils of a Traveler's life 
may gain experience in a similar manner to a Playable Character. 
For each level gained from accumulated Experience Points, the 
Tamed Creature rolls on the Creature Augmentations table.
If a creature rolls for an Augment that aligns closely with one it 
may have naturally, or it rolls a previous Augment, it may re-roll.

• Tamed Creatures have an amount of Hit Dice equal to their 
level. With dice that corresponds to their creature size: Small 1d6, 
Medium 1d8, Large 1d10, Huge 1d12, Gargantuan 1d20.
• If a Tamed Creature drops to 0 hit points, they are considered 
unconscious and are treated in the same manner as a Traveler in 
regards to Death Saving Throws and Stabilizing. 
• Reviving a creature, though unnatural, is possible with the 
Keepers discretion on the means to do so. If a cost is required, 
than it is recommend as a cost of 1000 GP x the CR Level (to a 
minimum of 1) of the creature.
Feral Instincts
Although there is a level of trust afforded to a Tamed creature, 
as control slips, their bestial nature takes over and they fall back 
to their instinctual behaviors. While not hostile to the Traveler 
or their allies, all control is lost until combat is complete or the 
Keeper deems it calm enough to retain control. On the creature's 
statblock, they will be labeled as one of three Feral Instincts.
Aggressive On its turn, the creature moves towards an enemy, 
attempts to attack and will not Disengage willingly from combat. 
If mounted, the Traveler may guide the creature towards enemies 
but may not force the creature to Disengage from combat.
Defensive The creature hunkers down or is to dim-witted to act. 
On its turn, the creature will refuse to move or attack, but can 
adopt any defensive abilities that it may have. If mounted, it will 
refuse to move but can fight back if attacked.
Wary On its turn, the creature attempts to flee from any enemies. 
If in combat, the creature will take the Disengage action, and 
move as far as possible from any aggressors. If mounted, the 
Traveler can guide the creature's direction of its flight, as long as 
its putting more distance between itself and its enemies.
Example: A CR 6 Grahknash with a Taming Level of 1 would need to 
accumulate 1200 xp before reaching a Taming Level of 2. 
Level 2 = 1200 xp (CR6 x 200)
